claims.text: In situ incorporation of h-BN into CoCrFeNi will reduce the coefficient of friction from room temperature to 800 °C relative to unmodified CoCrFeNi.
In situ incorporation of h-BN into CoCrFeNi will reduce wear rate from room temperature to 800 °C relative to unmodified CoCrFeNi.
The intervention will form a lubricious h-BN-containing tribofilm at the sliding interface.
The h-BN-containing tribofilm will remain continuous and persistent throughout sliding from room temperature to 800 °C.
h-BN reduces the interfacial shear strength.
The h-BN-containing tribofilm prevents direct metal-to-metal contact.
The thermal stability of h-BN ensures tribofilm persistence at elevated temperatures.
Reduced interfacial shear strength and metal-to-metal contact will lower both friction and wear.
The modified composite will exhibit a coefficient of friction below 0.3 across the full tested temperature range.
The modified composite will exhibit more than a 50% reduction in wear rate relative to unmodified CoCrFeNi across the full tested temperature range.
Unmodified CoCrFeNi has higher friction and wear, especially at elevated temperatures, because it lacks a lubricious tribofilm.
The intervention is expected to be effective in air and inert atmospheres where h-BN remains stable.
The intervention will cease to be effective when applied loads exceed the mechanical integrity of the tribofilm.
Above 800 °C or in strongly oxidizing atmospheres, h-BN may degrade and lose effectiveness.
Friction and wear reductions depend on the distribution, volume fraction, and stability of h-BN in the matrix.
Insufficient h-BN dispersion or inadequate tribofilm formation may limit performance.
The proposed comparison uses modified and unmodified CoCrFeNi samples tested under identical reciprocating-sliding conditions in air from room temperature to 800 °C.
